title: Noise-resistant circadian oscillator (Vilar et al., 2002)
reference: Vilar JMG, Kueh HY, Barkai N, Leibler S (2002). Mechanisms of noise-resistance in genetic oscillators. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 99:5988-5992. doi:10.1073/pnas.092133899

alpha_R__FREE.note: basal transcription of the repressor gene, /h

delta_R__FREE.note: degradation of free repressor, /h; the parameter the paper lowers to 0.05 to reach the regime where the deterministic system has a stable fixed point and only the stochastic one oscillates, so the search crosses that bifurcation

gamma_C__FREE.note: sequestration of the activator by the repressor, /(molecule*h)

notes: The collection's noise-resistant oscillator, the complement of McKane_PhysRevLett2005: there a limit cycle exists only because of demographic noise, here a deterministic limit cycle survives molecular noise essentially undegraded. Two things make it hard. Replicate means of an oscillator decay toward a constant as trajectories dephase, so the later cycles in the 100 h window carry period jitter rather than amplitude, and the data's _SD columns grow with time accordingly. And delta_R is free over a range that contains the paper's Fig. 5 value of 0.05 /h, at which the deterministic system relaxes to a stable fixed point instead of cycling, so the objective landscape contains a Hopf bifurcation the search has to cross.
